solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Agent that calms closers of serious crime case (8)

indicatorNotes.closers of: a closer is what ends something, so the closers of two words are their last letters

blocks.note: last letters of seriouS and crimE
the dative is a grammatical case

annotation.surface: A detective's sedative helps them unwind after wrapping up a serious crime case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads as a police investigation, but it is the grammatical kind: nominative, accusative, dative and so on.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a calming drug is an agent whose whole job is to soothe.

entries.clue: Perhaps David Lammy danced in Commons for Reform (6,2,7)

indicatorNotes.for Reform: the letters are offered up to be re-formed, rearranged into a new shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: A politician is imagined dancing in the House of Commons in support of the Reform party.
annotation.walkthrough: David Lammy became Deputy Prime Minister in 2025, so he is an example of a second-in-command; 'Perhaps' flags the example. 'Reform' borrows the name of the UK party Reform to hide the rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: As Deputy Prime Minister, David Lammy is second in command to the Prime Minister.

entries.clue: Head of demolitions returned explosive material (5)

indicatorNotes.Head of: the head of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.returned: sent back, so the word runs from right to left

blocks.note: first letter of Demolitions
a mine is an explosive device, turned round to ENIM

annotation.surface: A demolition boss comes back with explosives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Explosive material' reads as one phrase, but the split falls between them: 'material' is the definition, cloth.
annotation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton material, the stuff of jeans.

entries.clue: Piece from Louvre in chiselled granite frame (8)

indicatorNotes.Piece from: only a small piece, the first letter, is taken from the word
indicatorNotes.in: the L goes inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.chiselled: granite that has been chiselled has been reshaped

blocks.note: first letter of Louvre
anagram fodder, rearranged to TRIANGE with the L set inside

annotation.surface: An artwork from the Louvre is displayed in a frame carved from granite.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Frame' looks like part of a picture frame at the Louvre; it is the definition. 'Piece' also tempts as the definition, since a triangle is a percussion instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: A triangle is the frame used to rack up balls in pool or snooker.

entries.clue: Bottles short serf brought up filled with Iodine (5)

indicatorNotes.short: the word is cut short, losing its last letter
indicatorNotes.brought up: in a down entry, brought up means written bottom to top
indicatorNotes.filled with: the reversed word has I put inside it

blocks.note: a serf is a slave; SLAVE cut short is SLAV, brought up to VALS
I is the chemical symbol for iodine, set inside the reversed serf

annotation.surface: Medicine bottles are filled with iodine by a servant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Vials are small bottles, usually for medicine.

entries.clue: Small sounds of the enemy advancing for supplies (6)

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
time is 'the enemy'; as it advances a clock goes tick-tock

annotation.surface: Faint noises of an approaching army while troops wait for supplies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' is time, as in the phrase 'time is the enemy', so its sound as it moves on is the tock of a clock, not marching feet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: goods held in reserve for later use.

entries.clue: Boards son put down in Hackney home? (6)

indicatorNotes.put down in: in a down entry, the S is moved down to the bottom of the word

blocks.note: a hackney is a horse, and a horse's home is a stable
s = son; the S at the top of the horse's home moves to the bottom

annotation.surface: Someone's son is put up for the night in a house in Hackney, east London.
annotation.walkthrough: Hackney is a London borough, but a hackney is also a breed of horse, which lives in a stable.
annotation.definitionFit: A board is a table, as in 'bed and board' or a boardroom's table.

entries.clue: He composed “Sweet Child” during lunchtime (9)

blocks.note: a cherub is a sweet, angelic child
in = during, as in 'in the night'
lunchtime is one o'clock, and one is I

annotation.surface: Someone wrote the song 'Sweet Child' over a lunch break.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet Child' in quotes suggests the Guns N' Roses song; it is just a cherub. Luigi Cherubini was an Italian composer of operas and sacred music.
annotation.definitionFit: Cherubini was a composer, so 'He composed' describes him.

entries.clue: Lead can? (9,2,2,2)

blocks.note: a lead in an investigation, a clue that lets detectives proceed
the can is slang for the toilet, a seat one uses

annotation.walkthrough: The can is slang for the toilet, and the question mark admits the joke. 'Lead can' looks like a metal container.
annotation.definitionFit: A lead gives investigators something to go on; a toilet is something to go on in another sense.

entries.clue: Uninspiring role featuring in performance (8)

indicatorNotes.featuring in: the role features inside the other word

blocks.note: a deed is a performance, something performed
a part is a role in a play; it sits inside DEED

annotation.surface: A dull role in a stage show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uninspiring' looks like 'dull', but read it as un-in-spiring: no longer breathing in, so dead.
annotation.definitionFit: The departed are the dead, who no longer breathe in.

entries.clue: Person who runs an addict about to get drug (9)

indicatorNotes.about: the letters are turned about, rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, rearranged to CANDIDAT
E = ecstasy, the drug, added at the end

annotation.surface: A dealer hands drugs to an addict.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Person who runs' sounds like a drug runner in this surface; it is someone running for office.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Runs' is the election sense: someone standing for office.

entries.clue: One scaled girder to secure rivets at the top (5)

indicatorNotes.to secure: the girder holds the R fast inside it
indicatorNotes.at the top: only the top letter of the word is used

blocks.note: a girder is a steel beam
first letter of Rivets, held inside the girder

annotation.surface: A steelworker climbs a girder to fix the rivets at its top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One scaled' reads as someone who climbed the girder; it means a creature with scales, a fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A fish is covered in scales, so 'one scaled' describes it without naming it.

entries.clue: European flower on display in Wayne Manor (5)

indicatorNotes.on display in: the answer is openly shown inside the words that follow

blocks.note: wayNE MANor

annotation.surface: A flower is shown in the grounds of Batman's mansion, Wayne Manor.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows, a river. The Neman flows through Belarus and Lithuania into the Baltic.
annotation.definitionFit: The Neman is a river of eastern Europe.

entries.clue: Room (executive) for a high-flyer’s bodyguard? (9)

blocks.note: room = space, as in 'room to move'
suit is slang for a business executive

annotation.surface: An office is set aside for a VIP's security guard.
annotation.walkthrough: The high-flyer is an astronaut, not a business star, and the suit guards the body in a literal sense; the question mark flags the play.
annotation.definitionFit: A spacesuit protects an astronaut's body, so it is a bodyguard for someone who flies very high.

entries.clue: Show about the Spanish is in poor taste (10)

indicatorNotes.about: the word for show goes round, about, the other

blocks.note: to indicate is to show
el is 'the' in Spanish, set inside the word for show

annotation.surface: A TV programme about Spaniards is judged tasteless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a noun, a programme, but is the verb 'indicate'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tactless, coarse, lacking refinement.

entries.clue: Elated is how one could be after uninstalling Windows! (9)

annotation.definition2: how one could be after uninstalling Windows!

blocks.note: a plain synonym for overjoyed

blocks.clueFragment: how one could be after uninstalling Windows!
blocks.note: windows are lights, so removing them leaves you without lights

annotation.surface: Someone is overjoyed to have got rid of Microsoft Windows from their computer.
annotation.walkthrough: Windows is the Microsoft software in the surface, but here windows are lights, and taking out lights de-lights.
annotation.definitionFit: Delighted means very pleased, elated.

entries.clue: It taps in the morning around hill mostly close to Tulsa (8)

indicatorNotes.around: the morning goes round the hill
indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, its last letter dropped
indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taps are marked C and H, cold and hot
a.m., before noon
a rise is a hill; minus its last letter RIS, inside A(RIS)M
last letter of TulsA

annotation.surface: Someone tap-dances at dawn on a hill near Tulsa, Oklahoma.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun starting a sentence; it is the definition, 'it' meaning personal magnetism, as in 'she's got it'.
annotation.definitionFit: 'It' is the elusive appeal someone has, which is charisma.

entries.clue: National fruit (4)

blocks.note: a citizen of New Zealand, by nickname
the fuzzy green Chinese gooseberry, renamed after New Zealand's national bird

annotation.surface: A country's national fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun, a citizen of a country; Kiwi is the nickname for a New Zealander.
annotation.definitionFit: A Kiwi is a New Zealander, and a kiwi is a green fuzzy fruit.

entries.clue: Huge moon sure to be seen in a different light (8)

indicators: to be seen in a different light

indicatorNotes.to be seen in a different light: the letters are to be viewed differently, rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A big moon certainly looks different in changing light.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about moonlight, which suits the rearranging instruction perfectly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean very large indeed.

entries.clue: What you’ll hear announced in auction room (4)

indicatorNotes.announced: spoken out, so the answer sounds like the word

blocks.clueFragment: What you’ll hear announced in auction
blocks.note: an auction is where things sell

annotation.surface: What an auctioneer calls out in the saleroom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Auction room' looks like one phrase, but 'room' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery.

entries.clue: Old man moving in can and did upset German (3,7)

indicatorNotes.upset: the letters are knocked over and rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
G = German, joins the fodder

annotation.surface: A father's awkward moves upset a German guest.
annotation.walkthrough: Dad dancing is the British term for the embarrassing dance moves of middle-aged fathers at parties.
annotation.definitionFit: Almost literal: a father, the old man, moving awkwardly on the dance floor.

entries.clue: Chilled medium-sized chicken doesn’t need starter (6)

indicatorNotes.doesn’t need starter: the word goes without its first letter

blocks.note: M = medium, as on clothing labels
chicken = cowardly = YELLOW, minus its first letter

annotation.surface: A chilled mid-sized chicken can be cooked without a starter course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chilled' looks like refrigerated; it means relaxed. 'Chicken' is the adjective, cowardly, which is yellow.
annotation.definitionFit: Chilled, in slang, means relaxed, or mellow.

entries.clue: Two thousand seats supply seating for attraction (9)

indicatorNotes.seats: the two Ms give the other letters a seat between them
indicatorNotes.supply: read as 'supply' (in a supple way): the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two thousand is MM
anagram of SEATING, sat between the two Ms

annotation.surface: A stadium with two thousand seats needs seating supplied to attract fans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as the verb 'provide', but is the adverb from supple, flexibly; that is what tells you to rearrange SEATING.
annotation.definitionFit: Attraction in both the physical pull of a magnet and the personal sense of allure.

entries.clue: Maxim: married men should get a medal in the end (5)

indicatorNotes.in the end: only the end letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: m = married, as in genealogies
OR = other ranks, ordinary soldiers
surface padding joining the pieces
used as it stands
last letter of medaL

annotation.surface: A saying that married men should be awarded a medal eventually.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that surviving marriage deserves a medal; 'men' in crosswords is often OR, the other ranks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short lesson or rule for living.

entries.clue: Proportion of allowance patron finally cut (5)

indicatorNotes.finally: the last letter of the word
indicatorNotes.cut: to cut something is to remove it, so the N is taken out

blocks.note: a daily allowance of food
last letter of patroN, N, cut from the allowance

annotation.surface: A sponsor's share of the allowance is reduced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Proportion of allowance' reads as one phrase, a share; the definition stops at 'Proportion'.
annotation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses a proportion between two quantities.

entries.clue: Flipping lucre and ultimately godless vices? (5)

indicatorNotes.Flipping: the word is flipped over, written backwards
indicatorNotes.ultimately: the last letter of the word

blocks.note: loot is slang for money, lucre; flipped to TOOL
last letter of godlesS

annotation.surface: Money and godlessness as the root of all vice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vices' suggests sins, but a vice is a workshop clamp; the question mark admits the pun. 'Flipping' also works as a mild oath in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A vice is a clamping tool on a workbench, so vices are tools.

entries.clue: Russian co-op using some cellular telephones (5)

indicatorNotes.using some: only some of the letters are used

blocks.note: cellulAR TELephones

annotation.surface: A Russian collective relies on mobile phones.
annotation.walkthrough: An artel was a Russian workers' cooperative.
annotation.definitionFit: An artel is a Russian cooperative association of workers.

entries.clue: He travelled in company car east of ruin (5,4)

indicatorNotes.east of: in an across entry, east is to the right, so the company car comes after

blocks.note: to mar is to ruin or spoil
Co. = company
the Volkswagen Polo is a car

annotation.surface: A salesman drove a company car to the east, beyond some ruins.
annotation.walkthrough: Marco Polo was the Venetian merchant who travelled to China in the 13th century.
annotation.definitionFit: Marco Polo is famous as a traveller, so 'He travelled' describes him.

entries.clue: Wife in party hooked up with fellow cheat (2,4)

indicatorNotes.in: W goes inside the word for fellow
indicatorNotes.hooked up with: the party joins on in front

blocks.note: a do is a party
a don is a university fellow
w = wife, inside: DO(W)N

annotation.surface: A wife got together with another man at a party, cheating on her husband.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheat' reads as marital infidelity in the surface, but the definition means to swindle. To do someone down is to cheat or belittle them.
annotation.definitionFit: To do down means to cheat or get the better of someone.

entries.clue: Conservative is defeated with popular approaches (6,2)

blocks.note: C = Conservative, the British party
loses = is defeated
in = fashionable, popular

annotation.surface: A Tory loses an election while a popular rival draws nearer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the pieces in order.
annotation.definitionFit: To close in is to approach, draw nearer.
